title: Causal forest finds immunocompromised patients who benefit from high flow nasal oxygen
summary: A causal forest machine learning model derived in the HIGH randomized trial (704 analyzed patients) found no average HFNO effect on day-28 invasive mechanical ventilation but heterogeneous responses, from a predicted 20.2% absolute risk reduction with HFNO to a 7.4% reduction with conventional oxygen. The highest-benefit group had significantly fewer ventilations with HFNO. Benefit ranking held in an independent observational cohort of 818 patients, although absolute estimates were less calibrated; prospective confirmation is needed.
ai_technology: Causal forest machine learning for heterogeneous treatment effects
organization: Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris; Hôpital Saint-Louis

evidence.tested: Derivation in a randomized trial with bootstrap validation, and transportability testing in an independent observational cohort (n=818).
evidence.unknown: Subgroup finding from a post hoc analysis; absolute effects less calibrated externally; needs prospective validation; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Causal forest estimated individualized HFNO treatment effects from baseline characteristics.
